public.label: 01 / PUBLIC · EDUCATION & HUMAN CAPITAL
public.title: What would better learning actually look like?
public.desc: Education investment can produce new infrastructure without producing better learning. Programme design must identify how inputs become effective teaching, retention, inclusion and measurable skill gains.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
public.problemTitle: Inputs are visible. Learning is not.
problems: Access and quality vary across communities
Equipment and training do not guarantee classroom use
Costs are known; long-term value is uncertain
results: Link investment packages to learning pathways
Specify outcome and equity indicators
Appraise returns, delivery feasibility and evaluation design

private.label: 01 / PRIVATE · EDUCATION SERVICES
private.title: Does a learning product improve capability—not just uptake?
private.desc: A training or education technology provider may count enrolments and active accounts while remaining uncertain whether students or workers actually improve their competencies.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Completion counts are treated as skill gains
Customer outcomes are poorly measured
Impact evidence is disconnected from product improvements
results: Define measurable competencies and usage pathways
Compare learner progress against a credible benchmark
Connect learning effectiveness to product choices

public.label: 02 / PUBLIC · WORKER HEALTH & SOCIAL IMPACT
public.title: Can better health access change workers’ lives?
public.desc: Worker-focused services need evidence on access, uptake, health outcomes and their links to job wellbeing—not only clinic visits or outreach volume.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Workers may face barriers to access and trust
Programme utilisation is not health improvement
Business and social outcomes are rarely evaluated together
results: Assess wellbeing and access with appropriate consent
Use credible programme and comparison evidence
Connect worker outcomes to sustainable service models

private.label: 02 / PRIVATE · EMPLOYEE WELLBEING
private.title: Is a factory wellbeing investment creating shared value?
private.desc: Employers considering worker healthcare or wellbeing benefits need to understand take-up, productivity, retention and worker outcomes before expanding a programme.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Needs differ across job roles and workers
Absence and retention metrics lack context
Social returns and business value are confused
results: Measure access, usage and worker experience
Compare productivity and retention trajectories
Protect privacy while testing business value

public.label: 03 / PUBLIC · RESILIENCE & EARLY WARNING
public.title: Does an early warning actually reach the last mile?
public.desc: Resilience investment requires more than equipment. Effective warning systems have to convert hazard intelligence into timely action by people at risk.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
public.problemTitle: Forecast systems do not guarantee action.
problems: Warnings fail to reach some exposed communities
Agencies have fragmented roles and protocols
Benefit streams and operations funding are unclear
results: Design last-mile information and response pathways
Connect costs and avoided-loss scenarios
Specify indicators, governance and financing

private.label: 03 / PRIVATE · CLIMATE RISK MANAGEMENT
private.title: Will resilience investment protect business continuity?
private.desc: Firms exposed to floods, heat or supply-chain disruption need decision-quality estimates of losses avoided, operational feasibility and worker protection.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Climate shocks are treated as one-off events.
problems: Exposure is not translated into operational risk
Alert procedures are rarely stress-tested
Adaptation investment competes with immediate budgets
results: Link hazards to downtime and economic losses
Design protocols with suppliers and workers
Test avoided-loss and continuity scenarios

public.label: 04 / PUBLIC · LIVELIHOODS & INCLUSION
public.title: When incomes rise, which opportunities become durable?
public.desc: Livelihood programmes should test whether support changes access to markets, earnings, resilience and inclusion—not just the number of producers trained.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Producer earnings fluctuate with markets and shocks
Skills and technology may not connect to buyers
Effects differ by gender, assets and location
results: Map market, income and resilience constraints
Track income and adoption with a comparison strategy
Identify who benefits and why

private.label: 04 / PRIVATE · INCLUSIVE VALUE CHAINS
private.title: Can an inclusive sourcing model sustain higher incomes?
private.desc: Agribusinesses and social enterprises need to learn whether supplier support improves producer income while strengthening quality, reliability and long-term supply.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Training is not linked to producer margins
Procurement conditions are uneven
Benefits may bypass smaller or poorer suppliers
results: Track producer net income, not merely revenue
Measure reliability and upgrading costs
Adjust sourcing based on distributional evidence

public.label: 05 / PUBLIC · TECHNOLOGY & BEHAVIOUR
public.title: Why does promising technology fail to spread?
public.desc: A technology can be profitable on paper while businesses and workers remain reluctant to use it. Adoption research identifies the real incentives, frictions and information gaps.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Knowledge and finance constraints interact
Firms report technology but vary in effective use
Policies may overlook behaviour and firm heterogeneity
results: Identify barriers by firm and technology type
Test appropriately designed information or incentive responses
Measure meaningful use and productivity outcomes

private.label: 05 / PRIVATE · PRODUCT & PROCESS ADOPTION
private.title: Will a new production technology actually be used?
private.desc: Manufacturers and service businesses face an adoption gap between capital investment and sustained operational behaviour, especially when training and incentives are weak.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Purchasing technology is confused with using it.
problems: Workers and managers face different incentives
Operations do not capture baseline capability
Initial uptake may not survive implementation
results: Segment users and identify adoption friction
Pilot with measurable operational outcomes
Scale only after identifying successful practices

public.label: 06 / PUBLIC · INSTITUTIONS & REFORM
public.title: Can policy reform make public services work better?
public.desc: Changing a regulation is not itself a development outcome. Reform needs evidence that citizens and enterprises experience faster, fairer and more reliable service.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Processes remain fragmented after policy changes
Administrative data are hard to compare
Users experience delays and unequal treatment
results: Measure time, cost, access and user experience
Verify changes through administrative and field data
Link evidence to process and governance redesign

private.label: 06 / PRIVATE · ORGANISATIONAL IMPACT
private.title: Are management changes improving service delivery?
private.desc: A company or service provider may digitise processes and report milestones without knowing whether clients receive better, more inclusive and more efficient services.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Operational KPIs are disconnected from user needs
Efficiency may shift burdens onto customers
Teams lack a credible before/after comparison
results: Specify service-quality and inclusion outcomes
Track cycle times, costs and satisfaction
Use evaluation findings to redesign workflows
